title: Rehearsing We — what would it take for us to have a real say over the things we depend on?

voices.name: Sam
voices.text: Could we ask for the rota two weeks ahead? I know three people on my shift who want that, but I have not asked anyone on nights. Maybe they have different problems. I need to book childcare and at the moment next week's shifts go up on Friday. Last month I paid for a place I couldn't use because my hours changed again. The manager did swap a shift for me once, so I don't want to act as if she never helps. But having to ask for a favour every week is exhausting. I'm on extra hours now and I need the money. If we ask together, I want to know someone will back me up if my hours suddenly disappear. I would talk to the others during a break. I can't stay after work for meetings.

voices.name: Leah
voices.text: The woman upstairs knocked to ask whether our bedroom wall was wet too. That was the first time I knew it wasn't just our flat. We'd both been told to open the windows more. She's got photographs going back a year; I keep forgetting to take them until I've cleaned the mould off. We started a group chat, but the woman downstairs doesn't use it and her son answers the door for her. I haven't worked out how to include her. Someone suggested we all stop paying rent. Perhaps that would make the agent reply, but I moved twice before getting this place and I'm frightened of having to do it again. I could put the repair requests together and send them with everyone's name on them, if people wanted. I can do that this weekend. I don't know whether another email will change anything. The agent already knows the damp is there.

voices.name: Chris
voices.text: We got more than six hundred signatures about the evening bus and nothing changed. I helped collect them, so I'm a bit tired of being told to start a petition. The last service now leaves before my dad has finished his tea. He says I should go, but then he has the whole evening on his own. A taxi home costs more than I can keep paying. Apparently there was a consultation. I found the page afterwards and it asked which of three cuts people preferred. Keeping the service wasn't an option. I don't want to organise a volunteer bus. I want the people paid to run it to explain what it would take to restore it, with figures we can question. I'd go to that meeting. I might be angry at it, though, and I don't want someone deciding that means I'm not being constructive.

voices.name: Nadia
voices.text: We did get the school club to change its collection time once. Two mums asked everyone what they could manage and took the answers in. It made a real difference to me. One of them has stopped doing it now because people rang her about every little problem, including things she couldn't change. I hadn't realised how much time it took. Now the club has moved to another site and collection adds half an hour to my day. The school says most parents are happy. Maybe most are, but I don't know who they asked. I'd make a few calls if we decided to ask again. Tell me how many, though. I'm not agreeing to be the next person everyone phones.

voices.name: Ben
voices.text: I don't know most of the other riders. You see people outside the same restaurants, but if an order comes in you leave halfway through talking. The app cut what it pays for longer deliveries last month. There was a notification and a link to help, which just gave me the same information again. Some riders said we should all log off on Friday evening. I stayed on. I needed that day's money, and I don't know how many people actually joined in. I feel bad saying that because it probably makes it harder for everyone. If there was money to cover a day off, I might do it. But who would put it in, and who would decide what each person got? I haven't got spare money to contribute regularly. I'd rather meet a few people first than send my details to someone announcing a fund in a chat. I know that sounds slow when the pay has already changed.

voices.name: Rosa
voices.text: In our housing co-op we replaced the cleaning company and the new one is much better. We could change the contract ourselves. I like that, and I wouldn't go back to having a landlord if I could help it. But choosing someone to repair the boiler took weeks because nobody wanted responsibility for getting it wrong. I don't think a vote fixes every decision. Someone with experience could choose the contractor within an agreed budget. We would need to see what they'd spent. At the moment the same three people know how all the accounts work. When I asked about the service charge, they sent me a spreadsheet. I couldn't follow it, and then I felt awkward asking again. One of them offered to go through it with me, but only during the day when I'm working.

voices.name: Alex
voices.text: Please don't make the answer that families should take turns doing the care. I'm already filling in when my mum's visits are late. She needs help getting up, so a different time isn't a small change. I've had to leave work twice this month. When I phone the company they say the council hasn't paid for enough time, and the council tells me to speak to the company. I'd like to compare notes with other families, but I can't take on organising a group. If someone could stay with Mum, I could come to a meeting. She should have a say as well. People keep asking me what she needs when she's sitting right there.

voices.name: Mo
voices.text: I'd help with the library again if there was a clear job. Last time there were hundreds of messages and then everything went quiet. I never found out whether anyone met the council. I still go on Tuesdays to use the computers, so I could ask people there about the proposed hours. That would feel useful. I don't want to join three more chats. There was an argument about putting another campaign's slogan on our leaflets, and after that I couldn't tell what my name was being used to support. I agreed about keeping the library open. I didn't agree with everything everyone said, and I don't think I have to. Maybe the people doing most of the work felt they should decide. I can understand that, but then tell us what the decision is and let us say whether we're part of it. Even if we lose, I want someone to tell me what happened.
